input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
input.rationale: Section 22.1 gives Vendor unlimited, unannounced audit rights plus remote access to our systems — squarely in walk-away territory and failing the fallback on frequency, notice and system access. Sections 22.2 and 22.3 already meet the preferred position on cost allocation (Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%), no direct system or unrelated data access, and confidentiality of findings, so the minimal fix is to rewrite 22.1 to add once-per-12-months frequency, 30 days' written notice, business-hours conduct, an independent confidentiality-bound auditor, and deletion of the remote-access language.

proposal.summary: Limit Vendor audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, with no access to our systems.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We can accommodate usage verification, but not unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems: our position is one audit per 12 months on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and no access to our systems (consistent with Section 22.2). If helpful, we can accept 15 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.oldText: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
ops.newText: Vendor may audit Customer's use of the Services no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during Customer's normal business hours and without unreasonable disruption, using an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations. The audit will be conducted through records and reports Customer provides, and Vendor and its auditor have no right to access Customer's systems remotely or otherwise.
